correctness.rationale: The 24 signed permutations of (1+sqrt(2),1,1) yield 48 length-2 edges of degree four. Intersecting the 4 vertex-sign lines with 0<w<v<1 gives six exhaustive convex cells; exactly the all-negative cell has 8 crossings and the others 12. The octagon region is x>(1+sqrt(2))y+z. Its spherical triangle has angles pi/4, theta, theta, theta=acos(1/sqrt(5+2sqrt(2))), hence Haar probability 24theta/pi-9; moments follow. Independently constructed the 48-edge graph and tested 2999 generic directions with no rule disagreement. Finite direction tests corroborate, while exact clipping argument supplies the all-directions proof.
